Publish.LongDescription:
# Custom Zones
**Make your own zones and choose exactly which buildings grow in them.**
A custom zone is painted like any other zone and grows with the city's normal demand, but only the buildings you picked can appear in it. Want a street of red-brick row houses only, a farm belt without factories, or a downtown of glass towers? Make a zone for it.
**Beta:** this is a test version, and it touches how your city grows, so your feedback matters. If something looks wrong, please post in the **discussion** of this page (also reachable from the game's mod menu) with what you did and your log file: Cities Skylines II, Logs, CustomZones.log. Ideas are welcome there too.
## Quick start 1. Open the **zoning tool**. In the tool options, next to **Custom Zones**, click the button to open the panel. 2. Click **New zone** and choose the game zone it behaves like: low, row, medium or high density residential, mixed housing, commercial, industrial or office. 3. In the building list, **click the buildings you want**. A tick shows they are in the zone. 4. Pick your zone in the **Custom Zones tab** of the zoning toolbar and **paint it along roads**, like any other zone.
Picking a zone in the toolbar also selects it in the panel.
## The building list - **Click a card** to add the building with all its levels. Click it again to remove it. - **The numbers 1 to 5** under the picture are its levels. Click one to add or remove only that level. Hover a number to see that level on the card. - **Filled:** this level is in the zone. - **Outlined:** the level shown on the picture. - **Dim:** the building has no such level. - **A red warning** means the city does not need what it sells or makes right now, so it will not grow yet. - **Filters:** type, lot width and depth, height, level and source (base game or mods), plus a search box. - **In this zone** shows only the buildings you picked. **Can grow now** shows only the ones the city wants right now. - The buttons above the filters **add all shown**, **remove all shown** and **reset the filters**.
## The large preview Click the **magnifier** on a card to see the building big, with all its levels. - Zoom with the mouse wheel and drag to look around. - Step through the list with the arrows, and press 1 to 5 to change the level. - **This level grows in this zone** (Space) adds or removes the level you are looking at. **All its levels** (A) adds or removes all of them. - The round button **places the building in the city**, so you can see how it looks. Press Escape to come back.
## The zone window Click the **pencil** next to a zone. - **Name, colour and icon.** Use a game icon, one of your saved icons, or design your own (see below). - **Behaves like:** the game zone whose demand it uses. - **Growth**, **Level up** and **Prefer same design**: how buildings start and level up (see the next sections). - **Warnings** tell you when something is missing: - lot widths no building fits (those lots stay empty); - nothing can be born (no starting level ticked); - lot sizes where buildings stop levelling up, and at which level (tick more levels or buildings of that size to let them go higher); - why nothing is growing right now (no free lots, nothing fits, no demand, or the spot scores too low). - **Statistics** for this city: painted cells, buildings, households and workers. - Buttons to **export**, **duplicate** and **delete** the zone. Deleting unzones its painted cells, like erasing zoning in the game.
## Levels in short In the game, buildings start small and **level up** over time when they are well looked after. A higher level means a bigger or nicer building, more homes or jobs, higher rent and upkeep, and jobs that need more education.
Many buildings have their own look for each level. Some reuse the same look for two levels (the large preview shows "Level 2 = L1"), and a few only exist at a high level.
## Growth: two ways **Like the game (default).** New buildings start at **level 1** and go up **one level at a time**. When the game levels a building up, it becomes one of the buildings you ticked **for the next level**. If you ticked nothing for that level that fits the lot, the building stays where it is. Tick level 1 of a building so it can appear at all.
**Prefer same design** (on by default, only for "Like the game") decides which building it becomes: - **On:** it keeps its look when you ticked its own next level. Only when you did not, it becomes another building you ticked for that level. - **Off:** it becomes any building you ticked for the next level, at random, like the game does with all its zones. Good for a varied, mixed street. - Example: you ticked red brick houses at levels 1 to 3 and a glass block at level 3. With the option on, a red brick house at level 2 becomes the red brick level 3. With it off, it may become either.
**Skip levels.** Each building **keeps its own look**. It starts at the **lowest level you ticked** and levels up to its **next ticked level**, skipping the ones you did not tick. For example, tick 1, 3 and 5 and it goes 1, 3, 5. It never turns into a different building. This also lets you use buildings the game only has at a high level. - Skipping is **not a shortcut**: the building waits as long as the game would take for the levels in between. - **Mind the economy:** a building that starts above level 1 asks for that level's rent from day one, and its jobs need better educated workers. In a young or poor city it may struggle or stay empty.
**Level up** (on by default): turn it off and buildings in this zone keep the level they were born with forever. Other zones keep levelling up as usual.
## Level buttons in the building panel Select any zoned building (in a custom zone or a normal game zone) and its info panel gets two buttons: - **Level up:** the building goes up a level right now. In a custom zone it follows the zone's Growth and Prefer same design settings, and it works even when "Level up" is off there, because you asked for it. In a game zone it becomes a building of the next level, like the game would choose. - **Choose level:** a small list of levels 1 to 5, next to the panel. Pick one to turn the building into that level now, **up or down**. Its own design is used when it has that level; otherwise another building of that level (one you ticked, in a custom zone). Levels it cannot become are dim: there is no building of that level that fits the lot, makes the same goods, has a home for every household living there and is low enough for that spot. So **residents always keep their home**. - **Jobs change with the level**, just as in a normal level-up: higher levels want more educated workers, lower levels fewer and less educated ones, so some workers may have to find another job. - These changes are instant and skip the waiting, so use them as a design tool. Buildings marked **historic** are never changed. - Turn the buttons off in the options if you do not want them.
## Icon designer Draw a zone icon in the style of the game's zone icons. Start from one of many models, then change the shape, roof, facade, ground, trees, colours and dozens of details. **Save** the ones you like: they stay in your icon library for every zone.
## Sharing zones - **Export** one zone from its window, or all of them with the import button at the top of the panel. - To **import**, put a zone file in the exports folder (the options have a button to open it) and pick it in the import list. - Buildings from assets you do not have are kept in the zone but never grow.
## Options - **Keep buildings placed by hand** (on by default): growable buildings you place yourself (with the placement tool, Find It or similar) are not condemned while the zone under them stays the same. - **Level buttons in the building panel:** show or hide them. - **Open the exported zones folder.** - **Clear the icon library.**
## Strongly recommended: Building Icon Generator Custom Zones works on its own, but **Building Icon Generator** (by the same author) gives every building in the list and in the large preview a real full colour picture. Without it, buildings the game has no icon for get a plain grey drawing.
## Good to know - **Demand is never changed.** The mod only reads it. Buildings grow with the same rules as the game's own zones, so nothing grows when the city does not need it. - **Milestones still count.** Buildings of a zone your city has not unlocked yet do not grow, even in a custom zone, until you unlock it. The zone window tells you when this happens. - **Lots must fit.** The game cuts a zone into lots 1 to 6 or more cells wide. A lot only gets a building if your zone has one of that exact width. The zone window warns you about missing widths. - **Condemning works like the game.** Changing the zone under a building, or removing it from the zone's list, condemns it if it no longer fits. - **Your zones are kept between cities.** Every city can use them.
## Compatibility - **Do not use it with other mods that change how zones grow** (other custom zone mods). - **Plop the Growables** works together with it. - **Before removing the mod**, delete your custom zones in each city where you painted them (the zone window unzones their cells).
